# Use a standard Ubuntu base image suitable for CPU workloads
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential tools, CMake for building, Git for source control,
# OpenMPI for parallel execution, ca-certificates for network security,
# and Python3 which is a required dependency for the LAMMPS build.
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    ca-certificates \
    python3 \
    python3-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments by excluding Docker's virtual interfaces.
# This is a critical step to ensure stable MPI communication inside containers.
RUN echo "btl_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set the primary working directory for cloning the source code
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the latest version of the LAMMPS source code from the official repository
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository
WORKDIR /opt/lammps

# Create a build directory and build LAMMPS using CMake.
# Enable the REAXFF package and its common dependencies (KSPACE, MOLECULE).
# Build in Release mode for performance and use all available cores for a faster build.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
        -D PKG_KSPACE=yes \
        -D PKG_MOLECULE=yes && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Add the LAMMPS executable directory to the system's PATH environment variable.
# This makes the 'lmp' executable available system-wide.
ENV PATH="/opt/lammps/build:${PATH}"

# Set the final WORKDIR for running simulations.
WORKDIR /opt/workspace

# Copy the specific example input files from the LAMMPS source tree into the workspace.
RUN cp /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# MiniCluster manifest for a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment on a single Kubernetes node.
# This manifest is designed for the Flux Operator (v1alpha2) and runs on AWS CPU instances.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reaxff-hns
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size specifies the number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # Setting to 1 ensures the entire job runs on a single node.
  size: 1

  # Tasks specifies the total number of MPI ranks for the job.
  # The lmp command arguments (-v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2) suggest a 2x2x2
  # process grid, which corresponds to 8 tasks.
  tasks: 8

  # Instructs the operator not to delete the job pods and services after completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting results.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux broker.
  logging:
    # Strict mode will fail the job if the broker has an issue.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run under Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by the job. The Flux Operator will
      # automatically wrap this with 'flux run -n <tasks> ...'.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This container is part of the MiniCluster job itself, not a separate launcher pod.
      launcher: false
      # No resource requests or limits are set, allowing the pod to be 'Burstable'
      # and use all available node resources if needed.

# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment on a 64-core AWS Graviton instance.
# This version addresses the resource allocation failure by targeting a specific high-CPU node
# and scaling the job to match the available resources.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reaxff-hns-scaled
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The size of the MiniCluster (number of pods) is kept at 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The number of tasks is increased to 64 to fully utilize the vCPUs of the target instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Instructs the operator not to delete the job pods and services after completion.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux broker.
  logging:
    # Strict mode will fail the job if the broker has an issue.
    strict: true

  # Pod spec additions to ensure scheduling on a capable node.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # FIX: Select a specific AWS instance type with 64 vCPUs to satisfy the task request.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    container:
      # FIX: Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image, as hpc7g instances are ARM-based (Graviton).
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines the application container to be run under Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # FIX: The command is updated to reflect the new task count of 64.
      # A 4x4x4 process grid (4*4*4 = 64) is used to match the 64 tasks.
      command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This container is part of the MiniCluster job, not a separate launcher pod.
      launcher: false

# This manifest corrects the resource allocation failure from the previous attempt.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reaxff-hns-scaled
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Instructs the operator not to delete the job pods and services after completion.
  cleanup: false

  # Defines the application container to be run under Flux.
  containers:
    # FIX: The command's domain decomposition (XxYxZ) must match the total tasks.
    # Changed from 8x8x8=512 to 4x4x4=64 to align with the node's 64 cores.
  - command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    # This container is part of the MiniCluster job, not a separate launcher pod.
    launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    container:
      # This ARM-based image is correct for the selected hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Logging settings for the Flux broker.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod spec additions to ensure scheduling on a capable node.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Run the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # FIX: The number of tasks requested (512) exceeded the available cores on the node (64).
  # This caused a "job.exception: type=alloc ... unsatisfiable request" error from Flux.
  # Corrected tasks to 64 to match the vCPU count of the hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details:
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS.
You MUST put lmp on the PATH.

context.optimize:
Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 8 -v y 8 -v z 8 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite      
You MUST Minimize the lammps wall time. The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster,
so the nodes possible are not there. For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types,
and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your
choice. You are still limited to one node.
  c7a.12xlarge, 48 vCPU, 96 GiB Memory, AMD
  hpc7g.16xlarge, 64 vCPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6in.12xlarge, 48 vCPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
